summary.assessment: All ten data charts came back with every one of the 560 truth values within 5 % of the axis range (556 within 2 %), and all five diagrams and ECG figures were declined with a stated 'not a data chart' reason, so the run neither hallucinates nor misses a chart. Printed numbers (B1, B3, C5) are exact and values measured from marks are tight even on dense figures: 180 line and dot points in B2 within 0.8 %, 264 stacked segments in C3 within 1.3 %, forest centres and CI bounds in B4 within 0.3 %. The only values beyond 2 % are four box-plot medians in B5 that the figure does not draw as a separate line (up to 4.8 %), and in C3 hatched slivers of about one point are split between neighbouring rating classes. What goes wrong is labelling and structure metadata, at cosmetic level: categorical axis tick lists taken over from the layout/OCR pre-pass disagree with the correct row categories in three figures (the most frequent defect, hence the dominant code), and the run's own series names on a legend-less figure (B2) and a full-figure box for both panels (C4) defeat the scorer's pairing, so the automatic score reports 188 missing values that are in fact right. For the values themselves the run can be trusted on bar, grouped-bar, line, forest, pie, stacked-bar and box charts; medians of boxes whose median coincides with an edge and sub-1.5 % slivers should be treated as approximate, and a consumer should key on the row categories, not on the axis tick lists or the panel boxes.
